summary: Iteration 62 — Google Sheets lead-import integration. Backend pytest: 13/13 pass (test_iteration62_google_sheets.py). Verified: (1) /api/google/status returns {configured:true, connected:false} for both super_admin and office_admin without crashing; (2) /api/google/connect as super_admin returns a well-formed accounts.google.com authorization_url with access_type=offline, prompt=consent, redirect_uri ending in /api/oauth/sheets/callback, and a state param; office_admin also allowed (per _require_admin), staff → 403; (3) All Google data endpoints (/spreadsheets, /spreadsheets/{id}/worksheets, /spreadsheets/{id}/values, POST /template) correctly return 404 'Google account is not connected' with NO 500s when unconnected; (4) POST /api/google/import returns 404 for bogus campaign_id, and with a valid campaign correctly reports created_count/duplicate_count/invalid_count/duplicates/invalids — dedup by phone within payload works, empty-name rows counted as invalid; (5) /api/oauth/sheets/callback with error param or missing code/state returns 302 → /settings?google=error (no 500). Frontend UI: super_admin Settings page shows the 'Google Sheets' card (data-testid=google-sheets-settings) with 'Sign in with Google' button (data-testid=google-connect-btn); clicking it navigates to accounts.google.com with the correct client_id, offline access_type, consent prompt, and preview backend redirect_uri. On Leads → CRM → Campaigns tab, opening the seeded 'LBS' campaign shows 'Import from Sheets' button (data-testid=campaign-import-sheets-btn) alongside 'Upload CSV'; clicking opens dialog (data-testid=campaign-import-sheets-dialog) which correctly shows the not-connected prompt (data-testid=sheets-not-connected) instructing the user to connect in Settings. Regression: super_admin + office_admin login OK, Settings + Leads/Campaigns load without functional console errors (only benign pre-auth 401s from AuthedImage + recharts width warnings, same as prior iterations).
critical_code_review_comments: routers/google_sheets.py::google_status hits db.google_connections for every caller (staff included). That's fine functionally but is an extra query on a hot path for non-admins who cannot use the feature anyway. Consider early-return {configured, connected:false} when user.role is not admin — saves one Mongo hit per settings page load per staff user.

routers/google_sheets.py::google_connect stores oauth_states without a TTL index. The row is only auto-deleted on successful callback via find_one_and_delete; if the user abandons the flow, the state row lingers forever. Add a Mongo TTL index on oauth_states.expires_at (created_at + 10min), or convert expires_at to an actual datetime and use expireAfterSeconds:0.

_credentials_for uses HTTPException 404 for 'not connected'. Semantically 409 or 428 would be more accurate ('precondition required'), but 404 is what the frontend + tests are contracted to, so leaving as-is is safest — just document it.

import_leads: the dedup 'existing' query loads up to 200k lead docs into memory (find(...).to_list(200_000)). For offices with large lead volumes this will spike memory and latency. Prefer an aggregation that projects phone→count into a set on the server, or bound the query by office+campaign scope more tightly; also consider a Mongo index on {office:1, phone:1}.

GoogleSheetsSettings.jsx reads ?google=connected|error from location.search — good. Ensure the query param is cleared from the URL after the toast fires (window.history.replaceState) so a manual refresh does not re-toast; verify in code if not already done.

CampaignImportSheetsDialog: not-connected state is text-only. Consider adding a direct 'Go to Settings' anchor (<Link to='/settings#google'>) inside the not-connected block so users don't have to hunt through the sidebar — reduces friction on first use.
